```{r Load and plot human challenge data individually}
# Set wd to "/Users/angela/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-WashingtonStateUniversity(email.wsu.edu)/Flu Research/Data_R"

# Mac directory
base_directory <- "~/OneDrive - Fred Hutch Cancer Center/IAV Data/Monolix/Truncated Fittings/Projects"

flu_data <- read.csv(file.path(base_directory, "flu_all_truncated.csv"),
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                     sep = ",")

IDs <- unique(flu_data[,"ID"])
head(flu_data)

library(grid)
raw_plots <- list()         
plot_counter <- 0 

# loop through the volunteers to generate individual plots
for(ID in unique(flu_data$ID)){
  
  # subset the data for current volunteer
  volunteer_data <- flu_data[flu_data$ID == ID,]
  
  # create the plot for each volunteer's observed data
  observed_plot <- ggplot(volunteer_data,
                     aes(x = time, y = viral_titer))+
              geom_point(color = "black")+
              labs( #axes labels
                x = "Days Post Infection",
                y = "log10(TCID50/ml)",
                title = paste(ID)
              ) +
              theme_minimal()+ 
              #x-axis label (days post infection)
              scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 10),breaks = seq(0, 10, by = 2))+
              #y-axis label (viral load log10)
              scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.5, 8),
                                 breaks = seq(0, 10, by = 1)
            )
  print(observed_plot)
}
```

```{r Define time}
time_grid <- seq(0, 8, by = 0.25)  # Every 12 hours from 0 to 8 days
```

# Trend curves of low and high shedders using LOESS
```{r Smoothing the AVG using LOESS}
# Calculate peak median = median at observed time points of high vs. low-shedders' data
pop_average <- flu_data %>%
  group_by(group_label, time) %>%    # grouping by high/low and time
  summarize(average = median(viral_titer, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# statistical data: peak viral load, day of peak, median peak of each individual
peak_data <- flu_data %>%
  group_by(ID, group_label) %>%         #grouping by ID and high/low
  summarize(
    peak_viral_load = max(viral_titer, na.rm = TRUE),         # peak viral load
    day_of_peak = time[which.max(viral_titer)],               # time of peak 
    average_peak = median(peak_viral_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# peak average of each group
peak_average <- peak_data %>%
  group_by(group_label) %>%
  summarize(
    peak_average = mean(average_peak),
    peak_median = median(average_peak),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# ---------- peak average ------ peak median
# high |       4.55                 4.25
# low  |       1.82                 2
print(pop_average)

##################################################################
## Optimize to find best span value such that the SSE between 
# regression and mean value at each time point is minimized
## Define objective function
##################################################################
calculate_sse <- function(span, data){
  # time grid
  time_grid <- seq(min(data$time),
                   max(data$time),
                   by = 0.8)
  
  # Fit LOESS with given span
  loess_fit <- loess(average ~ time, 
                     data = data, 
                     span = span)
  
  # Predict on original time points (not interpolated grid)
  predictions <- predict(loess_fit, 
                         newdata = data)
  
  # Calculate SSE between prediction and observed data
  sse <- sum((data$average - predictions)^2, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  return(sse)
}

##################################################################
optimal_spans <- list()
sse_results <- data.frame()

for(group in unique(pop_average$group_label)){
  
  #subset data 
  group_data <- pop_average %>% filter(group_label == group)
  
  #optimize span (between 0.1 and 1) using previously defined function
  optimization <- optimize(
    f = calculate_sse,          # set the objective function
    interval = c(0.1, 1.0),     # interval for testing span values
    data = group_data,          # read in the subsetted data
    maximum = FALSE             # minimize instead
  )
  
  optimal_spans[[group]] <- optimization$minimum
  
  cat(sprintf("\n%s: Optimal span = %.3f, SSE = $.3f\n",     # to three decimal places
              group, optimization$minimum, 
              optimization$objective))
  
  # store results
  sse_results <- rbind(sse_results,
                       data.frame(group = group,
                                  optimal_span = optimization$minimum,
                                  min_sse = optimization$objective))
}

print(sse_results)

###################################################### 
# Low-shedders' smooth average using LOESS: locally estimated scatterplot smoothing
###################################################### 
low_smooth <- pop_average %>%
  filter(group_label == "Low-shedder") %>%
  {predict(loess(average ~time, 
                 data = ., 
                 span = 0.8
                 #span = 0.257
                 ),
           newdata = data.frame(time = time_grid))} %>%
  pmax(limit_of_detection) %>%         # take the max or LOD to avoid negatives
  data.frame(group_label = "Low-shedder",
             time = time_grid,
             average = .)

######################################################  
# High-shedders' smooth average using LOESS
###################################################### 
high_smooth <- pop_average %>%
  filter(group_label == "High-shedder") %>%
  {predict(loess(average ~ time, 
                 data = ., 
                 span = 0.8,
                 #span = 0.107
                 ), # span value between 0 and 1 controlling the amount of smoothing
           newdata = data.frame(time = time_grid))} %>%
  pmax(limit_of_detection) %>%         # take the max or LOD to avoid negatives
  data.frame(group_label = "High-shedder",
             time = time_grid,
             average = .)


###################################################### 
# Plot with smoothed averages using LOESS
###################################################### 
observed_loess_individuals <- ggplot()+
  
  # individual observations all in gray
  geom_line(data = flu_data,
            aes(x = time, 
                y = viral_titer, 
                group = ID),
            color = "gray70",
            alpha = 0.3,
            linewidth = 0.6)+
  
  # Low-shedders in red (LOESS)
  geom_line(data = low_smooth,
            aes(x = time, y = average, color = group_label),
            linewidth = 1) +
  
  # High-shedders in blue (LOESS)
  geom_line(data = high_smooth,
            aes(x = time, y = average, color = group_label), 
            linewidth = 1)+

  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Low-shedder" = "#E74C3C",
                                "High-shedder" = "#3498DB"),
                     # Legend labeling the median curves
                     name = "LOESS Curves") +
  
  # Facet by group
  facet_wrap(~group_label, ncol = 2, scales = "fixed")+
  
  # Labeling of plot
  labs(x = "DPI", 
       y = "Viral Titer",
       #title = "Human Challenge Data - Median Viral Load"    #median 
  ) +
  
  # Themes
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)+
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    legend.position = c(0.9, 0.88),     # top right position
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
  ) +
  
  # x-axis labeling
   scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 10), breaks = seq(0, 10, by = 2))+
  
  # y-axis labeling
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = expression(paste("Viral titer (log"[10], " TCID"[50], "/mL)")),
    breaks = seq(0, 7, by = 1),
    limits = c(0, 7)
  )

print(observed_loess_individuals)
```

```{r Low-shedder: Median with IQR}
# calculate summary statistics: median, q1, q3, mean for each cohort
pop_summary <- flu_data %>%
  group_by(group_label, time) %>%
  summarize(
    median = median(viral_titer, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(viral_titer, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(viral_titer, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(viral_titer, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# smooth median and IQR curves for low and high shedders pulling from 
# pop_summary

###------------ Low Shedders ------------ ###
# -- pop_summary df has "group_label" as "Low Shedders" and "High Shedder" 
# -- CASE SENSITIVE!!!

low_data <- pop_summary %>%
  filter(group_label == "Low Shedder")

low_shedders_smooth <- data.frame(
  group_label = "Low Shedder", 
  time = time_grid,
  
  # fit a smooth curve through time-specific medians 
  median = predict(
    loess(median ~ time, 
          data = low_data,
          span = 0.8),
    newdata = data.frame(time = time_grid) %>%
      pmax(limit_of_detection) %>%
      data.frame(group_label = "Low Shedder",
                 time = time_grid,
                 median = .)
  ),
  
  q1 = predict(
    loess(q1 ~ time, 
          data = low_data, 
          span = 0.8),
    newdata = data.frame(time = time_grid)
  ),
  
  q3 = predict(
    loess(q3 ~ time,
          data = low_data, 
          span = 0.8),
    newdata = data.frame(time = time_grid)
  )
)

### plotting low shedders
observed_low_shed <- ggplot()+
  
  # median
  geom_line(data = low_shedders_smooth,
          aes(x = time, 
              y = median, 
              color = "#E74C3C"),
          linewidth = 1) + 
  
  #Ribbon: use linetype = "dotted" if want dotted instead of ribbon
  geom_ribbon(data = low_shedders_smooth,
              aes(x = time, 
                  ymin = q1, 
                  ymax = q3), 
              fill = "#E74C3C",
              alpha = 0.5
              ) + 
  
  # Labeling of plot
  labs(x = "DPI", 
       y = "Viral Titer",
       title = "Low-Shedders: Median Viral Load"  
  ) +
  
  # Themes
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)+
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    legend.position = c(0.9, 0.88),     # top right position
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
  ) +
  
  # x-axis labeling
   scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 10), breaks = seq(0, 10, by = 2))+
  
  # y-axis labeling
  scale_y_continuous(
   # name = expression(paste("Viral titer (log"[10], " TCID"[50], "/mL)")),
    breaks = seq(0, 7, by = 1),
    limits = c(0, 7)
  )
          

print(observed_low_shed)
  
```
